title: feat(bookmarks): add widget title visibility and size controls
body:
Bookmarks headings were fixed at 11px, and the existing “Hide title” setting only affected individual bookmark names. Add a “Show widget title” toggle and an 8–32px heading-size slider. Existing widgets retain the visible 11px heading; hiding it preserves its text, and the bookmark layout accounts for the selected heading size. Rename the existing English label to “Hide bookmark names” to distinguish the controls.

Implements [the reported request](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/issues/6600#issuecomment-5707167747) and [the proposed controls](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/issues/6600#issuecomment-5708805969).

Validation: focused oxfmt and oxlint checks, translation JSON parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. Manually exercised the real Bookmarks component, option definitions, switch and slider inputs in an isolated browser fixture with mocked app data: 8px/32px bounds, heading hide/restore, preserved title text, and independent bookmark-name visibility. Full dashboard integration, typecheck, build and automated tests were not run.

title: bug: OIDC logout aborts the end-session request before it completes
body:
### Describe the bug

When you click “Logout” with `AUTH_PROVIDERS=oidc` and `AUTH_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL` pointing to Authentik's `end-session` endpoint, the network request is aborted (NS_BINDING_ABORTED in Firefox) because Homarr navigates back to the app before that cross-origin request completes. As a result, the IdP never processes the logout, and the SSO session remains active.

### Steps to reproduce

1.- Configure Homarr with OIDC + Authentik following the official SSO guide.
2.- Log in via OIDC.
3.- Log out from Homarr.
4.- Try logging in again. You are automatically logged in without being prompted for credentials.
5.- In DevTools Network, the request to .../end-session/ has no status code or response headers. NS_BINDING_ABORTED appears in the console.

### Impact

The user's SSO session at the identity provider is never invalidated. Clicking "Log out" only clears Homarr's local session and the IdP still considers the user authenticated. Anyone who subsequently opens the IdP or another application connected to the same SSO session is signed back in without being prompted for credentials.

### Additional information

I'm using Homarr version 1.77.1

### Version

Other (describe in "additional information")

### Installation method

Docker Compose

### Browser

Firefox

title: bug: I can't switch between the dark and light themes
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi,

I'm having trouble switching between light and dark themes from my profile icon.
It doesn't do anything; it doesn't respond. It's turned black, and I want it to be white. I can't change it.

### Steps to reproduce

Go to the icon in the upper-right corner where the user profile is located. There, you can change the theme, select a language, and log in. Or, if you're already logged in, your preferences will appear. In either case, changing the theme doesn't work. The result is the same with other browsers, such as Edge and Firefox.

### Impact

The software works, but visually I can't set it to the light theme.

### Additional information

My environment:
- Ubuntu Server 26
- Portainer
- Homarr stack
- Connected to Active Directory via LDAP
- Version 1.77.1 (also happens with some earlier versions)

### Version

1.77.0

### Installation method

Docker Compose

### Browser

Edge (Chromium)

title: feat(plex): surface newly added episodes in media releases widget
body:
Closes #6847

## Problem

`PlexIntegration.getMediaReleasesAsync()` only reads `/library/recentlyAdded`, which returns **seasons** with the season's own `addedAt`. Episodes added to a season that already exists never change that value, so the media releases widget never shows them (the widget looks stale for anyone following ongoing shows).

## Change

- Additionally fetch the most recently added episodes of every `show` library (`/library/sections/{id}/all?type=4&sort=addedAt:desc`, one request per show library, 50 items each).
- Seasons already in `/library/recentlyAdded` that received newer episodes are bumped to the episode's `addedAt` and use its `originallyAvailableAt` as release date.
- Seasons that fell out of `/library/recentlyAdded` but got new episodes are rebuilt from the episode metadata (`grandparentTitle` / `parentTitle`, `grandparentThumb` + `art` as images, link to the season).
- Result is sorted by `addedAt` desc and capped at 50 (Plex's default page size), so the widget behaves like Plex's own "Recently added" and like the Jellyfin integration (`Items/Latest` groups episodes into their series).
- Any failure while fetching episodes is logged and falls back to the previous behaviour, so servers/tokens without library access are unaffected.
- Small refactor: `fetchJsonAsync()` helper shared by the JSON endpoints, `recentlyAddedItemSchema` extracted so it can be reused.

## Tests

- Existing spec unchanged and passing (episode fetch fails in its mock → fallback path).
- New spec: bumped season ordering + release date, season rebuilt from episode metadata (title, images, href), and fallback when the episode endpoints error.

`pnpm --filter @homarr/integrations typecheck`, `lint` and `vitest run packages/integrations/src/plex` pass.

title: feat(plex): media releases widget should list newly added episodes, not seasons
body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

The Plex "Media releases" widget never shows new episodes added to an existing season.

`PlexIntegration.getMediaReleasesAsync()` calls `/library/recentlyAdded`, which returns **seasons** (type `season`) with the season's own `addedAt`. Adding episodes to a season that already exists does not change that value, so the season never moves up and the widget looks stale.

Example from my server (Plex 1.42, Homarr 1.77.1):

```
/library/sections/1/all?type=4&sort=addedAt:desc   (episodes)
09-14 09:19 | Futurama | Oceans Three
09-14 09:19 | Special Ops: Lioness | Kiss the Girls

/library/recentlyAdded   (what Homarr uses, newest first)
09-09 13:41 | Cambio de marcha | Season 2
09-09 13:41 | Cambio de marcha | Season 1
```

Proposal: for show libraries, fetch episodes instead of seasons, e.g. `/library/sections/{id}/all?type=4&sort=addedAt:desc` (or `/hubs/home/recentlyAdded?type=4`, which is what the Plex apps use), and map them to `MediaRelease` with `type: "tv"`, title = `grandparentTitle`, subtitle = `S{parentIndex}E{index} – {title}`. Optionally group consecutive episodes of the same season added in the same scan.

Related: the widget also uses `originallyAvailableAt` as `releaseDate`, so an old title added yesterday sorts/labels as old. Using `addedAt` (or exposing both) would make "recently added" match what Plex shows.

### Additional information

Related past issues: #3885, #3692, #6083 (all about season handling in this widget).

### fastify vulnerable to X-Forwarded-* spoofing under trustProxy hop-count
[CVE-2026-16732](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-16732) / [GHSA-3m5p-2c4r-xxw2](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3m5p-2c4r-xxw2)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

The fix for [CVE-2026-3635](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-3635) ([GHSA-444r-cwp2-x5xf](https://redirect.github.com/fastify/fastify/security/advisories/GHSA-444r-cwp2-x5xf)) added a `proxyFn(socket.remoteAddress, 0)` guard on the `X-Forwarded-*` reads in `request.host`, `request.protocol`, `request.hostname`, `request.ip`, and `request.ips`. That guard closes the IP, CIDR, and custom-function forms of `trustProxy` correctly because those forms compile to predicates that inspect the connecting address. The hop-count form (`trustProxy: <number>`) compiles to a predicate that structurally ignores the address argument, so the guard reduces to `0 < tp`, always true for any `tp >= 1`.

Applications configured with `trustProxy: <number>` (documented as "behind N reverse proxies", `trustProxy: 1` being the canonical single-proxy setting) remain vulnerable. An attacker who can reach the Fastify origin directly, bypassing the front-facing proxy, can spoof the request fields exactly as in the unpatched version. Impact class matches the parent CVE-2026-3635: host injection in generated URLs, HTTPS-enforcement bypass, secure-cookie / CSRF-origin bypass, host-based routing and cache poisoning.

##### Patches

Patched in fastify 5.12.1. The numeric form of `trustProxy` is now disabled at runtime and removed from the TypeScript type union.

##### Workarounds

- Migrate to an IP / CIDR / custom-function `trustProxy` value that validates the connecting address. Custom functions must inspect the `address` argument, not only the hop index.
- Ensure the Fastify origin is only reachable through the trusted proxy chain (no direct network path).

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.1 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N`

### Auth.js: OAuth state, nonce, and PKCE check cookies are not bound to the provider that created them
[CVE-2026-73419](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-73419) / [GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

Auth.js stores the OAuth/OIDC anti-CSRF checks (`state`, `nonce`, and the PKCE verifier) in global cookies that are not bound to the provider that created them. On callback, a check value minted during a sign-in started with one provider can satisfy the callback for a different provider, because the stored cookie is not verified against the callback provider's identity (provider id, issuer, client id, or redirect URI). In a multi-provider app that allows account linking while logged in, this provider-confusion / mix-up condition can let an attacker link their account at a second provider to a victim's user.

##### Am I affected?

You may be affected if **all** of the following hold:

- You use `next-auth` `<= 4.24.14` or `>= 5.0.0-beta.1, <= 5.0.0-beta.31`, or `@auth/core` `<= 0.41.2`.
- You configure multiple OAuth/OIDC providers.
- You allow users to link additional providers while logged in.
- At least one configured provider's authorization request is observable by an attacker, and at least one target provider's callback can be satisfied without a PKCE verifier (i.e. it relies only on `state` or only on `nonce`).

You are **not** affected if you use a single OAuth provider, do not allow logged-in account linking, or all providers enforce PKCE.

##### Impact

- Account-linking confusion: an attacker can get their account at a target provider linked to the victim's Auth.js user, granting the attacker persistent sign-in to the victim's account through that linked provider.
- Exploitation requires luring the victim into starting a legitimate same-origin flow; it cannot be performed by cross-site request forgery alone, which reduces practical likelihood.

##### Patched version

The fix binds the OAuth check cookies to the provider/authorization flow that created them, so a callback cannot consume a check value minted for a different provider. Upgrade to the first releases containing this fix (pending; this advisory will be updated with exact patched versions before publication).

##### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately:

- Enable PKCE (`checks: ["pkce"]`, in addition to `state`/`nonce`) on every provider that supports it; PKCE blocks the practical code-swap variant because the attacker cannot observe the relying party's verifier.
- Avoid offering logged-in account linking across multiple providers where one provider is lower-trust or attacker-observable.
- Treat `events.linkAccount` as sensitive: add audit logging, user notification, or out-of-band confirmation so that any unexpected link is visible (defense-in-depth, not a root-cause fix).

##### Credit

Reported by @​Nadav0077. Thank you for the responsible disclosure.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.8 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`

---

### PostCSS: incomplete fix of GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q — attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL reads arbitrary .map files when `from` is unset
[CVE-2026-69153](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-69153) / [GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The fix for GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q added a guard in `lib/previous-map.js` `PreviousMap.loadFile()` that restricts an attacker-controlled `sourceMappingURL` (from a CSS comment) to a `.map` extension and, for untrusted maps, rejects `..` traversal and absolute paths. The traversal/absolute rejection is nested inside `if (cssFile) { ... }`. When PostCSS is invoked without the `from` option, `cssFile` is falsy and that branch is skipped, leaving only the `.map` extension check.

`PreviousMap` is constructed by `lib/input.js` whenever `pathAvailable && sourceMapAvailable` (under Node with source-map available), independent of `opts.from`/`opts.map` (the constructor returns early only for `opts.map === false`). So `postcss([]).process(css)` on attacker CSS reaches `loadFile` with `cssFile` undefined, and an attacker `/*# sourceMappingURL=/abs/path/x.map */` (or `../`-traversing path) is read via `readFileSync`. When the file is valid JSON, its `sources` (filesystem paths) and `sourcesContent` (source contents) are disclosed in the generated source map.

##### Affected code (v8.5.22 — the release carrying the GHSA-6g55 fix)

```js
// lib/previous-map.js
loadFile(path, cssFile, trusted) {
  if (!trusted && !this.unsafeMap) {
    if (!/\.map$/i.test(path)) {
      return undefined
    }
    if (cssFile) {                       // guard runs ONLY when `from` is set
      let relativePath = relative(dirname(cssFile), path)
      if (relativePath === '..' ||
          relativePath.startsWith('..' + sep) ||
          isAbsolute(relativePath)) {
        return undefined
      }
    }
  }
  this.root = dirname(path)
  if (existsSync(path)) {
    this.mapFile = path
    return readFileSync(path, 'utf-8').toString().trim()   // sink
  }
}

// loadMap(): untrusted annotation path, trusted=false; file === opts.from
} else if (this.annotation) {
  let map = this.annotation
  if (file) map = join(dirname(file), map)   // no `from` -> map stays the raw URL
  let unknown = this.loadFile(map, file, false)  // file undefined -> cssFile falsy
```

##### Proof of concept (verified on postcss 8.5.22)

```js
const postcss = require('postcss')
const fs = require('fs')

// a 'secret' sourcemap OUTSIDE any expected tree (stand-in for another project's .map)
const secret = '/tmp/pcpoc/secret_out_of_tree.map'
fs.writeFileSync(secret, JSON.stringify({
  version: 3, sources: ['/etc/REAL_PATH_LEAK'], mappings: '', names: [],
  sourcesContent: ['TOP_SECRET_abcdef']
}))

const css = 'a{color:red}\n/*# sourceMappingURL=' + secret + ' */'
const leaks = m => m && JSON.stringify(m.toJSON ? m.toJSON() : m).includes('TOP_SECRET_abcdef')

;(async () => {
  // A) NO `from`  -> guard skipped -> arbitrary absolute .map read + disclosed
  const a = await postcss([]).process(css, { map: true })
  console.log('no from   -> leaked:', !!leaks(a.map))   // true

  // B) WITH `from` -> guard active -> blocked
  const b = await postcss([]).process(css, { from: '/tmp/pcpoc/in.css', map: true })
  console.log('with from -> leaked:', !!leaks(b.map))    // false
})()
```

Observed output on postcss 8.5.22:

```
no from   -> leaked: true      # sourcesContent 'TOP_SECRET_abcdef' AND sources '/etc/REAL_PATH_LEAK' appear in result.map
with from -> leaked: false     # guard rejects the absolute path
```

`../` traversal (no `from`) also succeeds; non-`.map` targets (`.txt`, `?x=.map`, `#.map`) are blocked by the `.map` check. The tested build contains the GHSA-6g55 fix (`this.json = JSON.parse(...)` in `loadMap`, `consumer()` uses `this.json || this.text`), so this is a residual of that fix.

##### Impact

Arbitrary `.map`-file read (absolute path or `../` traversal) and disclosure of the target map's `sources` (local filesystem paths) and `sourcesContent` (source) into the generated source map, for any consumer that runs PostCSS on attacker-influenced CSS without a `from` option and exposes `result.map` (online CSS playgrounds, minify/lint services, string-input build steps). Bounded to files ending in `.map` that parse as JSON.

##### Suggested fix

Apply the traversal/absolute-path rejection to the untrusted map path regardless of whether `cssFile` is present (resolve against `process.cwd()` when there is no `cssFile`, and reject absolute paths and `..` escape in all untrusted cases), or refuse to load an untrusted external map when no base file is known.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

#### References
- [https://github.com/postcss/postcss/security/advisories/GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp](https://redirect.github.com/postcss/postcss/security/advisories/GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp)
- [https://github.com/postcss/postcss/commit/7beca139e70f9075c6b19700fcb00dd8033e5da8](https://redirect.github.com/postcss/postcss/commit/7beca139e70f9075c6b19700fcb00dd8033e5da8)
- [https://github.com/postcss/postcss/releases/tag/8.5.19](https://redirect.github.com/postcss/postcss/releases/tag/8.5.19)
- [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp)

This data is provided by the [GitHub Advisory Database](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database/blob/main/LICENSE.md)).
</details>

title: bug: MCP tools/list fails on invite_createInvite z.date() schema
body:
### Describe the bug

On the current `release/v2` source, an authenticated MCP `tools/list` request fails with:

```text
Date cannot be represented in JSON Schema
```

The HTTP request succeeds, but the response contains JSON-RPC error code `-32603`. MCP clients that depend on `tools/list` consequently receive no Homarr tools, even though server discovery succeeds and Homarr's web catalog displays all 124 tools.

The likely source path is:

1. `invite_createInvite` is MCP-enabled and defines `expirationDate: z.date()`:
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/9d857377c12d188a15ae5e3c8c97c3928d6cadd9/packages/api/src/router/invite.ts#L53-L75

2. Homarr precomputes `tool.inputSchema` with `unrepresentable: "any"`, but also retains the original Zod `inputValidator`:
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/9d857377c12d188a15ae5e3c8c97c3928d6cadd9/packages/api/src/mcp-tools.ts#L104-L115

3. The MCP protocol handler registers the original validator as `inputSchema: tool.inputValidator`:
https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/9d857377c12d188a15ae5e3c8c97c3928d6cadd9/apps/nextjs/src/app/api/mcp/_protocol.ts#L49-L58

`@modelcontextprotocol/server` converts registered schemas while generating `tools/list`. Zod considers `z.date()` unrepresentable in JSON Schema and throws by default:
https://zod.dev/json-schema#unrepresentable

This appears to be the same underlying Zod behavior reported in nestjs/swagger#3672, although Homarr does not use NestJS Swagger:
https://github.com/nestjs/swagger/issues/3672

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run Homarr from `release/v2` revision `9d857377c12d188a15ae5e3c8c97c3928d6cadd9`.
2. Configure a valid Homarr API key.
3. Confirm that MCP server discovery succeeds.
4. Submit a `tools/list` request:

```bash
curl -N -X POST "http://<homarr-host>:7575/api/mcp" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -H "ApiKey: <id>.<token>" \
  --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'
```

5. Observe HTTP 200 carrying this JSON-RPC error:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "error": {
    "code": -32603,
    "message": "Date cannot be represented in JSON Schema"
  }
}
```

### Impact

The Homarr application and browser-visible tool catalog remain operational, but schema-discovery-based MCP clients cannot load any of the 124 advertised tools. This blocks Board, Custom Widget, integration, Docker, and other MCP capabilities even though those schemas are otherwise valid.

There is no practical client-side correction because the exception occurs while Homarr generates the server's `tools/list` response. Temporarily excluding only `invite_createInvite` should allow the remaining 123 tools to be discovered while a proper date wire schema is implemented.

### Additional information

### Expected behavior

`tools/list` should return the complete tool catalog. One unrepresentable tool schema should not prevent clients from discovering every other valid tool.

For this parameter, the MCP wire representation could be an ISO 8601 date-time string that Homarr converts to a JavaScript `Date`:

```ts
z.object({
  expirationDate: z.iso.datetime().transform((value) => new Date(value)),
})
```

With Zod 4.4.3 this produces a JSON Schema input property with `type: "string"` and `format: "date-time"`, while still producing a `Date` after validation. This behavior was confirmed independently against Zod 4.4.3; a patched Homarr image has not yet been runtime-tested.

Registering the already-generated JSON-safe `tool.inputSchema` is another possible protection. A regression test that serializes every production MCP tool through `tools/list` would help prevent one invalid schema from blocking the complete catalog again.

### Environment

- Source revision: `9d857377c12d188a15ae5e3c8c97c3928d6cadd9`
- Zod: `4.4.3`
- `@modelcontextprotocol/server`: `2.0.0`
- Installation: Docker image built from source
- Browser: Not applicable; reproduced through the MCP HTTP endpoint

### Version

Other (describe in "additional information")

### Installation method

From Source

### Browser

Other (describe in "additional information")

title: feat: Add support for Unraid Storage Pools
body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Reference to bug report #5538

Feature request to add support for Unraid storage pools, current GraphQL query only queries the primary array for Unraid.

### Additional information

Looking at the code and running my own GraphQL queries, it looks like Homarr's Unraid integration only supports querying the Unraid primary array (traditional Unraid setup), but does not query pools.

Homarr does not have a full enough query to fetch or process data in a pool-only setup, it would need be updated to query extra fields under the array root field, including (most importantly) caches.

The caches field is for querying a storage pool that is not the primary array (or boot, or parity)

Something like this should be merged into the integration code, both to support setups where both the primary array is used as well as pools, or for pool-only setups:

`query { array { caches { id name device size status temp fsSize fsFree fsUsed type isSpinning } } }`

Worth noting that only the first disk in the pool actually reports the size, the others don't, so disks returning "null" under fsSize, fsFree, fsUsed should simply be ignored.

title: fix: respect color scheme in PWA manifest theme color
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the white Android status bar in the installed PWA when Homarr is in dark mode.

The PWA manifest (`/manifest.webmanifest`) hard-coded `theme_color: "#fff"` and `background_color: "#fff"`. Unlike the HTML `<meta name="theme-color">` tags (which already handle `prefers-color-scheme` correctly), the manifest spec does **not** support media queries — so installed standalone apps always got a white status bar, regardless of the user's color scheme. There is no existing setting for this; it was a bug.

## Changes

- **`apps/nextjs/src/app/manifest.ts`** — the manifest is now generated dynamically:
  - Resolves the user's color scheme via `getCurrentColorSchemeAsync()` (cookie → server default)
  - `light` → `#fff`, `dark` → `#242424` (matches the app's actual dark background)
  - `auto` → falls back to the `Sec-CH-Prefers-Color-Scheme` client hint when present, else `#fff` (previous behavior, no regression)
- **`apps/nextjs/next.config.ts`** — sends `Accept-CH: Sec-CH-Prefers-Color-Scheme` + `Vary` on `/manifest.webmanifest` so browsers opt in and send the hint on subsequent manifest fetches (helps `auto` users after the first fetch; Chrome re-fetches the manifest periodically while installed).

## Verification

Tested against the dev server:

| Case | `theme_color` |
| --- | --- |
| cookie: `dark` | `#242424` |
| cookie: `light` | `#fff` |
| cookie: `auto` + hint `dark` | `#242424` |
| cookie: `auto` + hint `light` | `#fff` |
| no cookie (server default) | `#fff` |

`Accept-CH` and `Vary` headers confirmed present on `/manifest.webmanifest`.

## Notes

- Existing installs pick up the fix when the browser re-fetches the manifest (periodically, ~24h) or on reinstall.
- Firefox for Android additionally has a known upstream bug (Bugzilla [1964220](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1964220)) where some versions ignore the manifest `theme_color` entirely — this PR is the correct app-side fix regardless.

title: fix(unraid): use metrics.memory utilization for RAM widget values
body:
## What does this PR do?
Fixes the Unraid Health Monitoring RAM ring reporting absolute values ~1024x too small (e.g. `0.01 GiB` on a system with ~12 GiB used) while the percentage stayed correct.

## Root cause
`getSystemInfoAsync()` computed total memory from `info.memory.layout[].size` and then derived used memory via `percentTotal`:

```ts
const totalMemory = systemInfo.info.memory.layout.reduce((acc, layout) => layout.size + acc, 0);
const usedMemory = totalMemory * (systemInfo.metrics.memory.percentTotal / 100);
```

`info.memory.layout[].size` can be reported in KiB on some Unraid versions, so the summed total (and thus the used value) is ~1024x smaller than reality.

## Fix
The same GraphQL query already retrieves `metrics.memory.total`, `available`, `used` and `free` — all documented as bytes in the `MemoryUtilization` schema. Compute memory from those directly:

```ts
const totalMemory = systemInfo.metrics.memory.total;
const usedMemory = Math.max(totalMemory - systemInfo.metrics.memory.available, 0);
```

`total - available` matches Unraid's own practical “System + Docker” memory-pressure calculation and its `percentTotal` value, so the ring percentage stays consistent with the absolute value.

The integration still returns raw bytes (`memUsedInBytes` / `memAvailableInBytes`); the widget already formats them with the shared `formatBytes` helper from `@homarr/common` (see `packages/widgets/src/common/number.ts` usage in `system-health.tsx`). No byte math was duplicated.

## Changes
- `packages/integrations/src/unraid/unraid-integration.ts` — compute RAM from `metrics.memory.{total,available}`; drop the `info.memory.layout` query field
- `packages/integrations/src/unraid/unraid-types.ts` — remove unused `info.memory.layout` schema
- `packages/integrations/src/unraid/test/unraid-integration.spec.ts` — regression tests (correct byte values + no negative used memory)

## Verification
- `pnpm turbo typecheck --filter=@homarr/integrations` ✅
- `oxlint` (0 errors) ✅
- `oxfmt` ✅
- New unraid tests pass (2/2)
- Full integrations suite: 294 passed, 12 skipped — only pre-existing flaky pi-hole network test failed, which passes on re-run and also fails on `dev`
- Widgets suite: 657/657 passed

Closes #6745

title: bug: Unraid health widget reports RAM in GiB approximately 1024x too small
body:
### Describe the bug

When the Health Monitoring widget uses an Unraid integration, the RAM ring displays an incorrect absolute value (for example, 0.01 GiB on a system with 31.1 GiB usable RAM). The ring's percentage is approximately correct (about 37-38%), so the problem is limited to the absolute byte value used by Homarr.

Expected behavior: the ring should display approximately 12 GiB used out of 31.1 GiB, or provide a visible percentage option.

Actual behavior: it displays 0.01 GiB while the ring/tooltip percentage is approximately 38%.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run Unraid 7.3.2 with the built-in Unraid GraphQL API.
2. Create an Unraid integration in Homarr using a read-only API key.
3. Add the Health Monitoring widget and select the Unraid integration.
4. Observe the RAM ring.

On the affected system, Unraid itself reports:
- Usable RAM: approximately 31.1 GiB
- Available: approximately 19 GiB
- Used: approximately 12 GiB
- Usage: approximately 38%

Homarr displays 0.01 GiB while drawing a ring of approximately 38%.

### Impact

The widget is still usable for CPU and disk monitoring, and the RAM percentage appears correct, but the prominent RAM value is misleading. A workaround is to replace the combined Health Monitoring widget with separate System Resources and System Disks widgets, using the percentage shown by System Resources.

### Additional information

Environment:
- Homarr 1.76.1, official Docker image ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:latest
- Image source revision: 0e51f745d3f8ec4006aba1a29d695594c0cb07df
- Unraid 7.3.2
- Chrome

Likely cause:

In packages/integrations/src/unraid/unraid-integration.ts, getSystemInfoAsync() calculates total memory from info.memory.layout[].size and then derives used memory from metrics.memory.percentTotal:

```ts
const totalMemory = systemInfo.info.memory.layout.reduce((acc, layout) => layout.size + acc, 0);
const usedMemory = totalMemory * (systemInfo.metrics.memory.percentTotal / 100);
```

However, the same GraphQL query already retrieves metrics.memory.total, used, available, and free. Unraid's MemoryUtilization schema documents those fields as bytes. Using the utilization metrics directly should avoid relying on physical DIMM inventory/layout reporting:

```ts
memUsedInBytes: systemInfo.metrics.memory.total - systemInfo.metrics.memory.available,
memAvailableInBytes: systemInfo.metrics.memory.available,
```

Using total - available also matches Unraid/Linux's practical memory-pressure calculation and the existing percentTotal formula.

title: feat: Ping health-check timeout is hardcoded and too short for slower endpoints
body:
**Describe the bug**

The app-tile "ping" health check (`sendPingRequestAsync` / `withTimeoutAsync`) uses a fetch timeout that appears to be hardcoded internally, with no way to override it per-app or globally. Any monitored endpoint that legitimately takes longer than this to respond gets permanently flagged as "down" even though it is healthy.

**Concrete example**

A Nextcloud AIO mastercontainer admin interface (`https://<host>:8080`) consistently takes ~7-8 seconds to respond to a plain request (confirmed via direct curl, reproducible every time) due to its own internal orchestration checks. Homarr's ping check aborts before that, logging:

```
error: Failed to send ping request url="https://<host>:8080"
AbortError: This operation was aborted
```

**Expected behavior**

Either a configurable timeout (per-app field on the app/tile config, and/or a global server setting), or at minimum a longer default, so tiles pointing at slower-but-healthy admin backends do not get permanently reported as failing.

**Environment**

- Homarr (Docker), latest as of 2026-08.

title: fix(weather): respect NO_EXTERNAL_CONNECTION in location search and surface weather data states
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6671 — weather widget showing "No integration data available" despite being configured.

## Root cause

Since the v1.75.0 refactor, `widget.weather.atLocation` returns `null` when the `NO_EXTERNAL_CONNECTION` env flag is set, but `location.searchCity` (the city picker in the widget settings) was never guarded. A user with `NO_EXTERNAL_CONNECTION=true` can search and select a city, yet every weather widget shows "No integration data available" — exactly the reported symptom. Before 1.75.0 there was no guard at all, which matches "worked in earlier versions".

## Changes

- `packages/api/src/router/location.ts` — `location.searchCity` now respects `NO_EXTERNAL_CONNECTION` and returns `{ results: [] }` without making an outbound request, consistent with weather/RSS/analytics routers.
- `packages/widgets/src/weather/component.tsx` — distinguishes query states:
  - loading → empty state (unchanged)
  - error → "Failed to load weather data" + Retry button
  - `null` (external connections disabled) → explicit "Weather data is unavailable because outbound connections are disabled"
- `packages/translation/src/lang/en.json` — new `widget.weather.error.{disabled,failed,retry}` keys
- Docs: weather widget page and `NO_EXTERNAL_CONNECTION` env-var page now mention location search is also disabled.

## Tests

Added `packages/api/src/router/test/location.spec.ts` and `packages/api/src/router/test/widgets/weather.spec.ts` covering both flag states. Verified: affected vitest suites (62 tests), `tsc --noEmit` for api + widgets, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`.

## Verification

Booted the published `v1.76.0` image with `DB_DIALECT=sqlite`:
- with `NO_EXTERNAL_CONNECTION=true`: `atLocation` → `null`, `searchCity` → results (bug)
- without the flag: both endpoints return data

title: fix(mcp): use request-derived base URL for OAuth login redirect and well-known discovery
body:
## Description

Fixes #6628 — MCP OAuth flows were unusable behind a reverse proxy.

### Problem 1: Login redirect used the internal container origin

The `/api/mcp/oauth/authorize` route redirect to `/auth/login` was built from `url.origin`, which resolves to the internal container hostname (`<container-id>:3000`) when Homarr runs in Docker behind a proxy.

MCP OAuth URLs now use the configured public `BASE_URL` when present. Deployments without `BASE_URL` retain the existing `x-forwarded-proto` / `x-forwarded-host` / `host` fallback.

### Problem 2: `/.well-known/oauth-*` discovery endpoints returned 404

Next.js's App Router does not route folders with a dot prefix, so the OAuth authorization-server and protected-resource metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` were unreachable. The folders were moved to `well-known/` and rewrites keep the public URLs working:

- `/.well-known/:path*` for RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 root and path-inserted discovery
- `/api/mcp/:transport/.well-known/:path*` for clients using endpoint-appended discovery

Both forms preserve the transport-specific resource or issuer identifier. The MCP `WWW-Authenticate` challenge advertises the matching RFC 9728 path-inserted metadata URL.

No new environment variable or public URL was added. The existing `BASE_URL` behavior is now documented explicitly for OAuth metadata and redirects.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused OAuth metadata tests pass
- [x] Next.js lint passes with no errors
- [x] Next.js typecheck passes
- [x] Docs lint passes with no errors
- [x] No new dependencies

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added OAuth metadata discovery through standardized `.well-known` endpoints.
  * Added CORS support for metadata requests, including preflight handling.
  * Improved MCP authentication responses with accurate resource paths and host information.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Corrected authentication redirects when using configured or forwarded host details.
  * Added clear errors for unsupported discovery paths.

* **Documentation**

title: fix(backup): prompt re-login after database restore and log restore errors
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6622 — restoring a `.zip` backup showed an empty board (or a contextless login redirect) until a manual hard refresh.

### Root cause
Homarr uses Auth.js with `session: { strategy: "database" }` (`packages/auth/configuration.ts`). Restoring a backup **replaces `db.sqlite` on disk**, which invalidates the current session. The old client code did a silent `window.location.reload()` after the progress animation, so users landed on an empty board or the login screen with no explanation.

### Changes
- **`database-restore-flow.tsx`**: after a successful restore, show an explicit "Restore Complete — session invalidated" panel and auto-redirect to `/auth/login` (plus a manual "Sign in now" button). Uses `window.location.assign` to a different URL so the browser cannot restore the stale board document from bfcache.
- **`use-backup-analysis.ts`**: log backup analysis failures to the browser console.
- **`api/backup/import/route.ts`** & **`api/backup/migrations/route.ts`**: route restore errors through `createLogger` + `ErrorWithMetadata` (console + Redis transports) instead of raw `console.error`, and wrap the temporary DB close so a close failure cannot 500 a successful restore.

### Test instructions
1. On `main`, export a backup (Settings → Tools → Backup & Restore).
2. Modify boards, then restore the backup.
3. Before: empty board / silent login redirect until a manual hard refresh.
4. After: clear "session invalidated" message, auto-redirect to login, boards render immediately after signing in.

Also verify restore error logging appears in the container logs (e.g. try restoring a corrupt/foreign ZIP).

title: refactor: switch to isolated nodeLinker and declare phantom dependencies
body:
## What

Removes `nodeLinker: hoisted` and migrates the monorepo to pnpm's default **isolated** linker, declaring all previously-ghosted ("phantom") dependencies explicitly.

### Why

`nodeLinker: hoisted` was hiding undeclared dependencies: dozens of packages import `dayjs`, `axios`, `dockerode`, `clsx`, `@mantine/*`, `undici`, etc. without declaring them, relying on hoisting to flatten them into the root `node_modules`. This:

- Made dependency hygiene untrackable (no signal when a dep is actually missing).
- Blocked pnpm's **global virtual store** (`enableGlobalVirtualStore`), which only works with the isolated linker — the key feature for making git-worktrees / multi-agent setups fast and disk-cheap.
- Required a `sed`-based linker-swap hack in the Dockerfile (pnpm/pnpm#5268) that is no longer needed.

### Changes

- **`pnpm-workspace.yaml`**: remove `nodeLinker: hoisted` (defaults to `isolated`), add 12 previously-ghosted modules to the catalog (`axios`, `csstype`, `node-fetch`, `ofetch`, `prosemirror-model`, `winston-transport`, `@tanstack/query-core`, `@types/node-fetch`, etc.).
- **40 package.json files**: declare every phantom dependency that was only resolvable via hoisting (including `@types/*` for `react`, `pg`, `dockerode`, `node-fetch`, `node-unifi`; `@types/node` everywhere the base tsconfig requires `types: ["node"]`).
- **Root `package.json`**: `dotenv-cli` (used by the `with-env` script but never declared) and `@types/node-unifi` (referenced by the base tsconfig path mapping).
- **`Dockerfile`**: drop the hoisted→isolated `sed` workaround for `pnpm fetch`; add `--force` to the offline install so native build scripts (e.g. `better-sqlite3`) actually run when the offline store would otherwise reuse a stale "already built" marker.

### Verification

- `pnpm turbo typecheck` → **0 errors** across all 37 workspaces.
- `pnpm lint` → 37/37, 0 errors.
- `pnpm lint:ws` (sherif) → passes.
- `pnpm test` → 1790 pass / 2 fail — the 2 failures (`pi-hole.spec.ts`, `manifest.spec.ts`) are **pre-existing on `dev`** (verified identical on the baseline hoisted checkout).
- Docker `--target builder` build → succeeds.

### Notes

title: bug: Pi-hole v6 / Plex integrations send unauthenticated periodic health-check requests, causing real 401s
body:
## Bug description

Pi-hole and Plex integration widgets make a periodic background request (roughly every 10 seconds) that is **completely unauthenticated** — no session cookie, no `sid`, no API token, no `Authorization` header of any kind — separate from the widget's normal, correctly-authenticated data-fetching calls. The target server correctly rejects these with `401`.

This is distinct from #6255 (a client-side rendering flicker with confirmed-healthy backend auth throughout) — this is a genuine unauthenticated HTTP request reaching the target server, captured with full headers at the reverse-proxy layer.

## Evidence

**Pi-hole (v6, two independent instances, both affected identically):**

Homarr's own logs show the integration's actual auth flow succeeding:
```
[info]: Received session id successfully module="piHoleIntegration" version="v6" integrationId="gnjivm8oq0t9e899g8z2oya8"
[info]: Tested connection successfully module="integrationTestConnection" integrationName="Pi-Hole1" integrationKind="piHole" integrationUrl="https://<redacted>/"
```

But our reverse proxy (Caddy) access log shows a **separate, periodic** `GET /api/info/version` request, every ~10 seconds, with these being the *complete* request headers (nothing omitted):
```json
{
  "method": "GET",
  "host": "<pihole-instance>",
  "uri": "/api/info/version",
  "headers": {
    "Accept-Encoding": ["br, gzip, deflate"],
    "Connection": ["keep-alive"],
    "Accept": ["*/*"],
    "Accept-Language": ["*"],
    "Sec-Fetch-Mode": ["cors"],
    "User-Agent": ["undici"]
  },
  "status": 401
}
```

No cookie, no `sid` query param, no auth header of any kind. Pi-hole v6 requires authentication on this endpoint, so it correctly returns 401.

**Plex (same pattern):** a periodic `GET /` to the Plex server root, also with no `X-Plex-Token` and no other auth, also 401.

## Environment

- Homarr image: `ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr`, tag `v1.75.0` (latest tracked at time of report)
- Deployment: Docker Compose, reverse-proxied through Caddy
- Two `pihole` integrations (both Pi-hole v6.x), one `plex` integration, all three exhibiting the same unauthenticated-periodic-call pattern
- `User-Agent: undici` on the failing requests indicates this is server-side Node.js code (Homarr's backend), not a browser-originated call

## Impact

Low functional impact (the widgets' actual data display appears to work via the properly-authenticated path), but this generates a steady stream of real HTTP 401 responses from the Homarr container — which is picked up as anomalous by any security monitoring watching for repeated auth failures (e.g. fail2ban-style tooling, CrowdSec, SIEM 401-rate alerting). Worth fixing so Homarr doesn't itself look like a credential-stuffing source to anything monitoring the network it's on.

## Suspected cause

A periodic health-check / "is this integration still reachable" probe that's implemented as a bare unauthenticated request, separate from (and not reusing credentials/session from) the widget's actual authenticated data-fetch path. Possibly the same underlying code path referenced in past release notes ("stale value in integration select" / integration health-check logic), just manifesting as a real 401 rather than a rendering glitch.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Pi-hole v6 integration (or Plex) in Homarr
2. Put the integration behind a reverse proxy with access logging enabled
3. Watch the access log for the target host — a `GET /api/info/version` (Pi-hole) or `GET /` (Plex) request recurs every ~10s with zero auth headers and gets 401'd
4. Confirm the widget's own "test connection" / initial auth flow succeeds independently (Homarr's own logs will show a successful session)

title: feat(app-form): suggest the icon of the app website in the image picker
body:
## What this adds

When an app has a URL, the image picker now offers the icon of that website as its first suggestion.

While the picker dropdown is open, the server is asked for the icon of the app URL. If one is found it appears in an "Icon of the website" section above the library results and can be selected with the mouse or the keyboard like any other image. It is a suggestion only, nothing is written into the field for you.

## How it works

`fetchFaviconUrlAsync` in `@homarr/icons` requests the page the app URL points to, reads its `<link rel="icon">` and `<link rel="apple-touch-icon">` declarations and picks the best one. Apple touch icons rank first because they are meant as app artwork, and the declared `sizes` attribute breaks ties within the same relation. Relative hrefs are resolved against the URL that actually answered, so a redirect to a login page still resolves correctly. When the page declares nothing usable, `/favicon.ico` of the origin is probed and only accepted when the response really is an image, because many self hosted apps answer unknown paths with their HTML entry point.

Details:

- The requests go through `fetchWithTrustedCertificatesAsync`, so self signed certificates of local apps are handled the same way as everywhere else in Homarr.
- Timeout of 5 seconds per request, at most 256 KiB of HTML is read, and reading stops at `</head>`.
- Only `http` and `https` are accepted, validated in the input schema and again in the fetcher. Local addresses are allowed on purpose, self hosted apps usually live on the same network as Homarr.
- The procedure requires the `app-create` permission, which every path that opens the app form already requires, and it returns `null` when `NO_EXTERNAL_CONNECTION` is set, like the other outbound procedures.
- Detection only runs while the dropdown is open, so typing a URL does not cause a request per keystroke.
- Everything fails quietly to `null`, an unreachable app simply produces no suggestion.

## Tests

- `packages/icons/src/test/favicon-fetcher.spec.ts` covers relation ranking, size ranking, resolution against the redirect target, the well known fallback, the HTML entry point false positive and rejected protocols.
- `icon-picker.spec.ts` covers that the suggestion is offered and selectable, and that detection stays disabled without a website or while the dropdown is closed.

## Context

This is a focused re-cut of the favicon detection half of #6248 against the picker from #6556. The pagination half of #6248 is obsolete since the rewrite covers it, and the old branch no longer applies. The detection is rebuilt for the new picker rather than ported: it hooks into the picker sections instead of writing the field, and it uses the trusted certificate fetch helper. #6248 can be closed.

title: feat(integrations): add Komodo integration
body:
## Summary

- add a native, read-only Komodo integration using API key and API secret authentication
- extend the existing **Containers** widget (`dockerContainers`) with Komodo as an optional data source instead of adding new widgets, as suggested in review
- show Komodo containers in the existing table, with a compact summary of server, stack, deployment, and problem counts above it
- add a **Servers** view to the same widget with CPU, memory, disk, load average, network throughput, core count, and Periphery version
- make the displayed sections and the 1-300 second refresh interval configurable
- document the integration and the extended widget

Leaving the integration selection empty keeps the widget on Homarr's direct Docker connection, unchanged.

## Implementation details

- follows the existing integration → request handler → tRPC router → widget layering
- reads containers via `/read/ListAllContainers`, falling back to `/read/ListAllDockerContainers` on older Komodo versions
- maps Komodo container states onto Homarr's Docker states and falls back to `unknown` for future states
- maps Komodo resource states to healthy, warning, error, and unknown without failing on future states
- excludes templates and keeps malformed individual resources visible as unknown where possible
- normalizes Komodo network deltas to bytes per second using the reported Periphery polling rate
- shares the container icon lookup between the Docker and Komodo paths
- performs only authenticated read requests and does not expose credentials to the client

## Behaviour changes

These are user-visible and affect existing boards:

- the widget is renamed from **Docker stats** to **Containers**, since it is no longer Docker-only. Non-English names follow via Crowdin.
- Docker actions (start, stop, restart, remove, logs, add to Homarr) are hidden when a Komodo integration is selected — the actions column is filtered out and the row context menu is disabled. Komodo is read-only; Homarr never mutates Komodo resources.
- query errors are now surfaced through the widget error boundary instead of being swallowed. On a public board, a viewer without admin rights now sees the "no permission" card rather than an empty table, because `docker.getContainers` requires admin.
- the Komodo-specific switches are marked `skipContextMenu`, so the widget right-click menu is not flooded with options that do not apply to a plain Docker widget.

title: feat(api): expand REST coverage for full dashboard automation
body:
Closes #6435.

## Why

Boards could only be created empty through the API. `POST /api/boards/items` took no geometry, so the size always came from `widgetDefaultSizes` and the position was always the next free cell — a dashboard could not be described in code. Search engines, integrations, groups, api keys and global settings were reachable from the interface only.

## Board composition

`POST /api/boards/items` now accepts an **optional** placement. Without it the behaviour is byte for byte what it was before:

```json
{ "boardId": "...", "kind": "clock", "sectionId": "...", "xOffset": 4, "yOffset": 2, "width": 6, "height": 5 }
```

`width`/`height` set the size, `xOffset`/`yOffset` an exact position, `sectionId` the target section. The values apply to every layout and the width is clamped to narrow breakpoints; a `layouts` array gives per breakpoint control instead. Overlaps are rejected with `400`.

Added around it:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Items | `GET /api/boards/{id}/items`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /api/boards/{boardId}/items/{itemId}` |
| Sections | `GET`/`POST /api/boards/{id}/sections`, `PATCH`/`DELETE .../sections/{sectionId}` |
| Layouts | `GET`/`PUT /api/boards/{id}/layouts` |
| Board | `GET /api/boards/{id}` returns layouts, sections and items at once |
| Access | `GET /api/boards/{id}/permissions`, `PUT .../permissions/users`, `PUT .../permissions/groups` |
| Portability | `GET /api/boards/{id}/export` ⇄ `POST /api/boards/import` with `onConflict: fail｜skip｜replace` |

Ids inside a board document are local references and are remapped on import, so the same document can be applied repeatedly and to other instances.

## Remaining services

Search engines, integrations, groups, api keys and server settings are exposed over OpenAPI and registered as MCP tools. `GET /api/config/export` ⇄ `POST /api/config/import` cover a whole instance.

The configuration document keeps ids as they are — widget options reference other entities by id inside an opaque object, so remapping would silently break boards. Entities are instead matched by natural key when the id is unknown, which is what makes a document from a separately installed instance applicable at all: every instance seeds its own `everyone` group with a random id.

It deliberately contains no users, no group memberships, no secret values, no custom widgets and no media — that is documented, and the backup endpoints remain the way to make a complete copy. Those now accept an `ApiKey` header so a recovery job does not need a browser session.

## Headless bootstrap

`homarr api-keys create -u admin` prints a key without the web interface. Together with the existing `recreate-admin` that removes the last manual step from a first time setup. `api-keys list` and `delete` are there too.

## Safety

- **No database migration.** The schema already stores position and size in `item_layout`.
- **Imports are atomic.** Statements are collected and validated first, then applied in one transaction, so a document with a broken reference never leaves a board half written. `replace` never deletes the board row, so home board settings and per user permissions pointing at it survive.
- **Bounded work.** Grid coordinates and sizes in a document are capped, and the placement scan only tests slot edges and never looks past the last occupied row, so its cost does not depend on the column count.
- **Backwards compatible.** Every new field is optional; existing endpoints keep their behaviour.

## Testing

`pnpm turbo typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm format` are clean, docs build passes. 377 tests in the touched packages, including:

- placement: explicit size and position, collisions, clamping to narrow breakpoints, dynamic sections as sub grids, regression on the previous automatic placement
- import/export round trips, `skip`/`replace` idempotency, rollback on an invalid document, cross instance adoption
- authorization: anonymous and unprivileged sessions against every new endpoint, asserting `404` rather than `403` where board existence must not leak

The ten failing files in a full run (`packages/db/test/*-migration`, `packages/integrations/test/*`) are testcontainers based and fail identically on a clean checkout here.

## Notes for review

- Documentation lives in `apps/docs` in this repo, so it is updated in tree rather than in `homarr-labs/documentation`. Happy to move it if that is the wrong place.
- `POST /api/boards/import` keeps the strict board name rule because it creates a board like the interface does; `config/import` accepts any name because it restores. Both are documented.
- The grid cap is 256. It covers oldmarr boards with room to spare, but if wider boards exist in the wild the number should be revisited.

# Homarr v2 release flight check

This PR is the single release checklist. Add evidence beside each completed gate; validate one frozen candidate, and repeat affected checks when it changes.

**Path:** finish fixes in `release/v2` → merge `release/v2` directly into `dev` → human-approved `dev → main` major release → verify public artifacts.

## Current state · 2026-09-12

- `release/v2`: `2049c6ade`; `dev`: `43a57a2d`; latest stable: **v1.77.1**.
- [Previously validated baseline CI and preview publication](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/actions/runs/34508074005), CodeQL and Workshop passed. This does **not** prove upgrade or browser behavior.
- Release article #6790 and llama.cpp #6765 are merged. #6806 remains excluded. #6810 is closed and is not a release prerequisite; its earlier focused browser results do not establish acceptance of the final release candidate.
- Direct merge path selected: `release/v2 → dev`. The branches currently have 65 dev-only / 606 v2-only commits. Their conflicts are resolved in #6821 (`0501c6f21`), which contains both current branch tips. Land that merge with dev ancestry preserved, then refresh the direct comparison. #6820 targets the old bottom stack and is not a prerequisite for this path.
- #6824 is merged: source setup, production update docs, beta workflow and demo username protection. #6821 now merges current `dev` as well as `release/v2`; refreshed CI is pending. Next.js, Widgets and Translation typechecks and 37 focused tests passed. Dev fixes, translations and exact-build regression-report fields remain for review.
- Check the [dev branch rules](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/rules/687872) against the direct merge PR: the previous audit found a retired `Container and E2E` requirement. Reconcile required checks before landing. Rules on the old `v2` stack branch are not a prerequisite for this path.

## Before release

- [ ] **Integrate and freeze.** Review and land #6821 after CI with its merge ancestry preserved; exclude #6806. Prepare the direct `release/v2 → dev` merge, resolve conflicts, and verify preserved dev fixes. Land the reviewed result in `dev`; record candidate SHA and release owner. The individual stack layers do not need to land first.
- [ ] **Pass release validation.** On that candidate, pass CI/CodeQL, docs/Workshop builds and both image architectures; reconcile required checks; attach a production dependency/image security report and resolve or explicitly accept release-critical findings.
- [ ] **Record data-safety evidence.** Attach the completed v1 → v2 automatic migration checks and database coverage, including representative data and sign-in. Repeat affected cases only if migration changes land. Keep backup/restore and rollback evidence with the release record; users update their image normally.
- [ ] **Check regressions against current dev.** Replay the same desktop/mobile flows and fixtures: login/permissions, boards and drag/resize, widget refresh/failure, integration setup, import/export and backup. Check v2-only Custom Widgets, Workshop, Assistant/MCP and onboarding separately. For each confirmed regression, link one issue with exact builds, reproduction steps, impact and an owner; check for duplicates and verify the same steps after a fix. Revisit open regressions and affected flows as release changes land.
- [ ] **Prepare publication.** Verify production image/Workshop URLs and Helm guidance; coordinate the GA article with artifact availability (docs deploy from `dev`, and the article is already marked `draft: false`); prepare release notes, support and rollback ownership. Confirm Semantic Release selects v2.0.0 and keep the major-release human merge gate.

## Release and follow-through

- [ ] **Release, verify and announce.** Human-merge the approved `dev → main` PR; verify the v2.0.0 release, archives and immutable amd64/arm64 image digests. Smoke a public clean install and v1 upgrade; verify docs, Workshop and downloads; then announce and monitor upgrade/auth/data issues with a named rollback owner.
